title: Compact-parameter operation for a contractive functional
statement:
Let $B$ be a normed field, let $X$ be a nonempty compact Hausdorff topological space, and give $C(X,B)$ its supremum norm. Suppose $L:C(X,B)\to B$ is $B$-linear and $|L(g)|\leq\|g\|_\infty$ for every $g\in C(X,B)$. For a profinite space $P$ (compact Hausdorff with a basis of clopen sets) and $f\in C(P\times X,B)$, put
$$J_P(f)(p)=L(x\mapsto f(p,x)).$$
For every $p_0\in P$ and $\epsilon>0$, there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $p_0$ such that for all $p\in V$,
$$\sup_{x\in X}|f(p,x)-f(p_0,x)|\leq\epsilon/2,\qquad |J_P(f)(p)-J_P(f)(p_0)|\leq\epsilon/2.$$
In particular $J_P(f)$ is continuous. With the action $(cf)(p,x)=c(p)f(p,x)$, this gives a $C(P,B)$-linear map $J_P:C(P\times X,B)\to C(P,B)$, and for every finite index set $T$ and family $(f_t)_{t\in T}$,
$$J_P\left(\sum_{t\in T}f_t\right)=\sum_{t\in T}J_P(f_t).$$
For every continuous map $u:P'\to P$ of profinite spaces,
$$J_{P'}(f\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_X))=J_P(f)\circ u.$$
Empty $P$, empty $P'$ and empty finite sums are allowed. No completeness or nonarchimedean hypothesis on $B$ is assumed. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Write $f_p(x)=f(p,x)$. The map $x\mapsto(p,x)$ is continuous, so $f_p\in C(X,B)$ and $J_P(f)(p)$ is defined. Fix $p_0$ and $\epsilon>0$. The function $h(p,x)=|f(p,x)-f(p_0,x)|$ is continuous: both arguments of the subtraction are continuous compositions, subtraction is continuous in a normed field, and the norm is continuous by the triangle inequality. Thus $W=\{(p,x):h(p,x)<\epsilon/2\}$ is open and contains $\{p_0\}\times X$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image scalar analytic input; agent expansion, compact-parameter functional argument, step 1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compact-product-open-neighborhoods] to the compact subsets $\{p_0\}\subseteq P$ and $X\subseteq X$ and the open set $W$ of step 1. A singleton is compact because one member of any open cover covers it; $X$ is compact by hypothesis. We obtain open $V\subseteq P$ and $O\subseteq X$ with $p_0\in V$, $X\subseteq O$, and $V\times O\subseteq W$. Since $O=X$, for all $p\in V$ and $x\in X$ we have $|f_p(x)-f_{p_0}(x)|<\epsilon/2$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image scalar analytic input; agent expansion, compact-parameter functional argument, step 2

proof.text: For $p\in V$, taking the supremum of the pointwise inequalities gives $\|f_p-f_{p_0}\|_\infty\leq\epsilon/2$: the number $\epsilon/2$ is an upper bound for every value. By linearity and contractivity, $|J_P(f)(p)-J_P(f)(p_0)|=|L(f_p-f_{p_0})|\leq\|f_p-f_{p_0}\|_\infty\leq\epsilon/2$. This proves both estimates. Since $\epsilon/2<\epsilon$, the neighbourhood $V$ proves continuity at $p_0$ by the metric definition. If $P$ is empty there are no points to check, and its unique $B$-valued function is continuous.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image scalar analytic input; agent expansion, compact-parameter functional argument, step 3

proof.text: Pointwise operations preserve continuity in the normed field $B$. In particular $(cf)(p,x)=c(p)f(p,x)$ is continuous, and the module axioms hold pointwise. For $f,g\in C(P\times X,B)$ and $c\in C(P,B)$, linearity of $L$ gives $J_P(f+g)(p)=L(f_p+g_p)=J_P(f)(p)+J_P(g)(p)$, $J_P(0)(p)=0$, and $J_P(cf)(p)=L(c(p)f_p)=c(p)J_P(f)(p)$. Function extensionality makes these identities in $C(P,B)$, so $J_P$ is $C(P,B)$-linear. Induction on the finite set $T$, starting from $L(0)=0$ and using the addition identity, proves the finite-sum formula, including $T=\varnothing$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct-image scalar analytic input; agent expansion, compact-parameter functional argument, step 4

proof.text: For continuous $u:P'\to P$, the product map $u\times\mathrm{id}_X$ is continuous. The section at $p'$ of $f\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_X)$ is literally $f_{u(p')}$. Hence $J_{P'}(f\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_X))(p')=L(f_{u(p')})=J_P(f)(u(p'))$. Both sides are continuous by step 3 and composition. Function extensionality gives the asserted equality, also when $P'$ is empty. None of these arguments uses completeness, a nonarchimedean inequality, or nonemptiness of the parameter spaces.
